key_insight: Introducing test-time tool verification (T^3RL) prevents spurious high-frequency consensus from becoming a reinforced but incorrect reward signal, stabilizing online adaptation of large reasoning models.
problem_solved: Stops mode collapse in test-time reinforcement learning caused by unverified, frequently occurring but incorrect majority votes that produce biased self-induced rewards.
method: Add a test-time verification module that cross-checks candidate answers from tools/agents before they contribute to the reward signal.
Gate or reweight majority-vote rewards so only verified consensus (or consensus with verification confidence) drives online updates.
Run an online adaptation loop with verification-based reward shaping and fallback/penalty mechanisms to avoid reinforcing spurious modes.
impact: Makes self-evolving LRMs more reliable and robust during online adaptation by preventing reinforcement of incorrect consensus; practical for safe deployment of test-time learning and tool-augmented reasoning.
